pr.title: perf(core): preserve numeric memo when updates leave dictionary unchanged
pr.body:
> 🤖 **SPARQ agent** — I am @jeswr's agent for the sparq-org/sparq RDF/SPARQL engine. @jeswr runs multiple agents; this was written by the SPARQ agent, not the PSS agent (prod-solid-server).

Updates that leave the dictionary unchanged currently discard the cached numeric-precision verdict. The next numeric-filter safety check then scans the dictionary again. This preserves the memo after deletions, known-term reinsertion and inline-integer insertion, while retaining invalidation when stored terms grow and the existing conservative high-precision verdict.

The change documents dictionary/cache coherence and covers dense, sparse, forked and mapped graphs, including compaction, snapshot isolation and WAL replay. It addresses #6485. The separate first cold scan in #3113 remains unchanged and that parent issue stays open.

Validation: four focused default tests and five mmap/dict-spill tests passed on the source commit `73769114f081c8455aa21a393d0b992bd1283b67`; four deliberate invalidation defects compiled and failed the expected behavioral assertions. Scoped Clippy with warnings denied and touched formatting passed. These are actual native Rust 2021 module builds using recorded dependencies, not a full workspace/wasm gate. Local preflight stopped at the established Bash 3 `mapfile` limitation; normal Linux CI remains required. No latency, throughput or heap improvement is claimed.

The final child `9ac4a59e96b1c69c8d617fbde9e98fe8c0436fed` adds only the numbered V2 intent declaration for this always-compiled optimization; the reviewed/tested Rust source is byte-identical. JSON validation, the existing declaration-checker self-tests and diff checks passed. This declares intent, not wasm byte neutrality. The normal feature-off comparison, independent wasm size ratchet, required CI and protected merge process remain unchanged.

Implementation: GPT-6 Astra with extra-high reasoning. Actual independent Claude Opus 5 with extra-high reasoning approved the source and metadata followup at the final head for normal CI, with no blocking findings. The proof covers both dictionary terms and cached numeric presence; the avoided scan performs numeric-cache lookups with conditional term checks. The issue remains open until the fix is on main and relevant post-merge evidence is checked.
